title: Site size had mixed target-evenness slopes at fixed source and target count in seven worm maps
abstract: We tested whether larger chemical synaptic sites have more even target fractions in seven public worm brain maps. We used full-site annotations from Witvliet et al. and held the source cell and distinct-target count fixed. The fitted evenness change per doubling of size ranged from -0.0540 to +0.0080. Five slopes were negative. Two negative slopes passed a seven-test Holm correction in within-group shuffle tests. No positive slope passed that rule. The adult negative slope did not retain its sign in a rank-based sensitivity fit. Thus the data did not support a common positive linear size rule in this selected sample. Image geometry, selected groups, one adult map, uncertain exchangeability and no matched activity limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence and a separate-data retrieval program support reproduction. External databases are not bundled.

display.caption: Fitted evenness changes per doubling of site size. Bars show nominal 95 percent source bootstrap sensitivity ranges. The section-count check is exploratory. Different maps are different animals.
